label: How much the next dollar does compared with a charity's past average (per charity)

rows.label: The Humane League: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Animal Charity Evaluators, The Humane League review (2025): room for more funding, cost-effectiveness and organizational health
source.note: Room 0.85: ACE finds THL can spend up to $28.7M a year in 2026-27, $4.4M above its projected $24.3M revenue; reserves above its nine-month target. Use 0.6: over 2,700 cage-free pledges already won and most due by 2024 met; the next dollar goes to the harder rest (companies that haven't implemented, over 40% due in 2025) and to newer regions ACE rates less certain. Run 1.0: ACE finds no decision-relevant concerns; a CEO change in 2025.

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with the past average our models of The Humane League start from: room (is money the constraint) × use (what the next dollar buys compared with the average) × run (how well the organisation is run): 0.85 × 0.6 × 1.0 = 51%, from 30% to 80%.

rows.label: Wild Animal Initiative: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Animal Charity Evaluators, Wild Animal Initiative review (2025): room for more funding and organizational health
source.note: Room 0.5: ACE finds WAI can spend up to $6.9M a year in 2026-27 (a gap of about $3M), but net assets were over twice its 2024 spending, above its 12-month target. Use 0.6: new money goes to fellows, university hubs, a prize and fundraising staff, some of which ACE rates only moderate. Run 1.05: independent board with public minutes, long-serving director, no major concerns.

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Wild Animal Initiative's past average: room × use × run = 0.5 × 0.6 × 1.05 = 32%, from 15% to 60%. Low on room: about two years of spending held in reserve.

rows.label: British Heart Foundation: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: British Heart Foundation, Trustees' report and accounts, year to 31 March 2025
source.note: Room 0.55: cash and investments £346.4M against a liquidity requirement of £142-176M; new grants fell from £119.3M to £108.4M; no stated funding gap. Use 0.7: no evidence on the marginal grant against the average (neutral). Run 1.0: stable leadership and a new strategy; no external assessment found (neutral).

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with the British Heart Foundation's past average: room × use × run = 0.55 × 0.7 × 1.0 = 39%, from 20% to 70%. Room is low: reserves well above what its trustees require.

rows.label: Sinergia Animal: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Animal Charity Evaluators, Sinergia Animal review (2025): room for more funding
source.note: Room 0.8: ACE finds it can absorb $6.6M a year in 2027-28 against 2025 revenue of $4.2M, a gap of about $2.4M; no reserves figure stated. Use 0.6: the average rests on large Latin American cage-free wins (51 new commitments since 2024); extra money goes to staff, more campaigning in the main countries and movement-building, where ACE gives no evidence of the same yield. Run 1.0: ACE reports a very strong track record; no leadership or turnover assessment on the page (neutral).

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Sinergia Animal's past average: room × use × run = 0.8 × 0.6 × 1.0 = 48%, from 28% to 75%. Money is clearly the constraint, but the biggest cage-free wins are already won.

rows.label: Aquatic Life Institute: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Animal Charity Evaluators, Aquatic Life Institute review (2024 version, 2025 recommendation): room for more funding and organizational health
source.note: Room 0.85: ACE finds it can use up to about $1.2M a year in 2025-26 against 2024 revenue of $650K; net assets about 45% of annual spending (roughly 5 months) and ACE advises larger reserves. Use 0.6: extra funds go to a fundraising officer, a certifier specialist and an alliance community manager, which add capacity rather than more of the modelled corporate and policy work. Run 1.0: no concerns, 5 independent board members, 100% of staff confident in leadership, engagement 4.9/5.

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Aquatic Life Institute's past average: room × use × run = 0.85 × 0.6 × 1.0 = 51%, from 28% to 80%. Money is the constraint, but new funds mostly buy staff and fundraising capacity.

rows.label: Animal Welfare Observatory: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Animal Charity Evaluators, Animal Welfare Observatory review (2025): room for more funding and organizational health
source.note: Room 0.65: ACE finds it can spend up to about $2.5M a year in 2026-27, about $0.7M above projected 2025 revenue; reserves about 45% of annual spending (roughly 5.4 months), within its own 5-7 month target. Use 0.6: new money goes to accountability work (only 2% of 653 ECC commitments reported fulfilled), a new shrimp campaign, systems and EU advocacy, not new pledges like the average. Run 0.95: no decision-relevant concerns, but the Executive Director stepped down in March 2025 after an internal review (new director September 2025) and there is no conflict-of-interest policy.

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Animal Welfare Observatory's past average: room × use × run = 0.65 × 0.6 × 0.95 = 37%, from 20% to 60%. Reserves sit at its own target, and new money goes to accountability and a new campaign.

rows.label: Çiftlik Hayvanlarını Koruma Derneği: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Animal Charity Evaluators, Çiftlik Hayvanlarını Koruma Derneği review (2026 evaluation): room for more funding
source.note: Room 0.8: ACE finds it can absorb about $2M a year in 2027-28 against 2026 revenue of $1M; reserves and expenses not stated. Use 0.6: new money goes to fish welfare research regranting, an egg certification scheme and accountability for the 11 cage-free commitments already won, not more cage-free pledges (the modelled work). Run 1.0: ACE says sound organizational health but gives no detail on leadership or turnover (neutral).

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Çiftlik Hayvanlarını Koruma Derneği's past average: room × use × run = 0.8 × 0.6 × 1.0 = 48%, from 25% to 80%. Room is large, but new money goes to fish research and certification, not the cage-free work the model prices.

rows.label: Sociedade Vegetariana Brasileira: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Animal Charity Evaluators, Sociedade Vegetariana Brasileira review (2025): room for more funding and organizational health
source.note: Room 0.55: ACE finds it can use up to $0.9M a year in 2026-27, $206K above projected 2025 revenue; reserves 43% of 2024 spending (about 5 months) against its 6-month target. Use 0.6: priorities are government advocacy, a larger campaigns and training team and nutrition staff, not more school meal replacement, which is the modelled work; ACE rates staff training and a psychologist moderate or lower. Run 0.95: no decision-relevant concerns and 86% of staff confident in leadership, but only 2 of 7 board members are independent, one is married to the President, and there is no conflict-of-interest policy.

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Sociedade Vegetariana Brasileira's past average: room × use × run = 0.55 × 0.6 × 0.95 = 31%, from 15% to 55%. The gap is small and reserves are near target, and new money funds advocacy more than meal replacement.

rows.label: The Nature Conservancy: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: The Nature Conservancy, consolidated audited financial statements, years ended 30 June 2025 and 2024
source.note: Room 0.4: FY2025 operating revenues and releases $1,804M against expenses $1,601M (a $202M operating surplus; FY2024 +$109M); net assets $8,602M; $988M of financial assets and credit lines available within a year (Note 2), about 7.4 months of expenses; no stated funding gap. Use 0.6: no evidence on the marginal project; most money goes to land, deals and policies where TNC is a small share of the resources, and the next dollar goes to the less proven branches. Run 1.0: no external assessment found (neutral).

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with The Nature Conservancy's past average: room × use × run = 0.4 × 0.6 × 1.0 = 24%, from 10% to 50%. Room is low: a large operating surplus and about seven months of spending in liquid assets.

rows.label: Breast Cancer Now: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Breast Cancer Now, annual report and accounts 2024/25 (year to 31 July 2025)
source.note: Room 0.8: spending £66.8M against income £59.3M, a £7.8M deficit (a £12M deficit was planned, funded from reserves); total funds £40.5M (about 7 months), of which £33.7M is designated for long-term research commitments and free reserves are £5.8M against a £8.9M sufficient level, so money is partly the constraint. Use 0.7: no evidence on the marginal grant against the research average (neutral). Run 1.0: a record income and a smaller deficit than budgeted; a new chief executive in the year (neutral).

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Breast Cancer Now's past average: room × use × run = 0.8 × 0.7 × 1.0 = 56%, from 30% to 85%. Room is fairly high: it spends more than it raises, with free reserves below its own sufficient level.

rows.label: Doctors Without Borders: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: MSF International Financial Report 2025, Treasurer's report
source.note: Room 0.5: 2025 operating surplus €105M (2024: €22M deficit), equity reserves €1,598M, 7.7 months of expenses (7.8 in 2024), liquid reserves 6.0 months; MSF says it was not directly hit by the aid cuts and that growing expenses require prudence. Use 0.8: demand rose where other aid stopped (Somalia, Sudan), and funds are largely unrestricted, but MSF also says it must be selective about new programmes. Run 1.0: no external assessment found (neutral); a combined audited report with a reserves policy.

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Doctors Without Borders' past average: room × use × run = 0.5 × 0.8 × 1.0 = 40%, from 20% to 70%. Room is moderate: more than seven months of spending in reserve, but spending is growing and need is rising.

rows.label: Habitat for Humanity: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Habitat for Humanity International, consolidated audited financial statements, year to 30 June 2025
source.note: Room 0.75: FY2025 revenues $383M against expenses $377M (change in net assets +$5M; FY2024 -$2M); net assets $447M, of which a board-designated operating reserve of $75M (about 2.4 months); $10M credit line; no stated funding gap. Use 0.7: no evidence on the marginal US affiliate home or repair against the average (neutral). Run 1.0: no external assessment found (neutral).

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Habitat for Humanity's past average: room × use × run = 0.75 × 0.7 × 1.0 = 53%, from 30% to 85%. Room is fairly high: revenue about matches spending and the operating reserve is only a couple of months.

rows.label: MND Association: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: MND Association, Trustees' report and accounts 2024
source.note: Room 0.55: income £40.8M against spending £33.9M (surplus £6.8M); unrestricted reserves £42.1M, above the policy ceiling of six months' spending (£22.8M), though £19.4M is designated for spending by 2028 and the charity says its work will cost at least £35M a year and aims for £50M income by 2030. Use 0.7: no evidence on the marginal grant against the average (neutral); record research commitment of £24.2M over 133 grants. Run 1.0: a new Director of Research and several new directors in 2024-25, no external assessment found (neutral).

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with the MND Association's past average: room × use × run = 0.55 × 0.7 × 1.0 = 39%, from 20% to 70%. Reserves are above the trustees' own ceiling, but spending is growing into them.

rows.label: Royal National Lifeboat Institution: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: RNLI, Annual Report and Accounts 2024
source.note: Room 0.45: free reserves £157.9M = 9.7 months of spending, at the upper end of the trustees' 4-10 month requirement (8.9 months in 2023); income available for charitable spend £246.9M against charitable spend £190.3M. Use 0.7: lives saved rose from 362 to 437 with launches flat (9,141), but nothing on the marginal station or boat against the average (neutral). Run 1.0: new chief executive in summer 2024, no major concerns reported (neutral).

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with the RNLI's past average: room × use × run = 0.45 × 0.7 × 1.0 = 32%, from 15% to 60%. Reserves sit near the top of the trustees' range and income exceeds spending.

rows.label: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: St. Jude and ALSAC, combined financial statements, fiscal year 2024
source.note: Room 0.3: total net assets about $11.3B at FY2024 (up from $10.2B), against costs of more than $2 billion a year: several years of spending in reserve, still growing. Use 0.7: no controlled outcome published for any branch (neutral). Run 1.0: no external assessment found (neutral).

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with St. Jude's past average: room × use × run = 0.3 × 0.7 × 1.0 = 21%, from 10% to 50%. Room is the floor: several years of spending already held in reserve, with money still being added to it.

rows.label: Versus Arthritis: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Versus Arthritis, Trustees' report and accounts, year to 31 March 2025
source.note: Room 0.6: free reserves £56.9M against a target of £27.8M (twelve months' budgeted spending excluding research awards), but income fell 5.4% to £30.0M against spending £40.9M, a deficit of £10.9M before investment gains; planned spending has exceeded income since 2019 and it aims for a balanced budget from 2027/28. Use 0.7: £16.6M of new research awards in 2024/25 (2024: £9.1M), no evidence on the marginal grant (neutral). Run 0.95: a structural deficit for six years and a restructure; no leadership concerns found.

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Versus Arthritis's past average: room × use × run = 0.6 × 0.7 × 0.95 = 40%, from 20% to 70%. Reserves are twice its target, but it is spending them down to cover a deficit.
